slides.title: Why exactly **16,384** slots? Not 65,536?
slides.text: The answer is hiding in the heartbeat 👉

slides.title: Every heartbeat carries the **slot map**
slides.text: Nodes gossip constantly. Each ping includes a bitmap: 1 bit per slot.
slides.barsNote: size of the slot bitmap in every PING / PONG

slides.title: Big headers = **wasted bandwidth**
bullets: 📡|Hundreds of nodes ping each other nonstop
📦|8 KB headers on every message add up
🗜️|The bitmap compresses badly when nodes own many slots

slides.title: Cluster is built for **~1,000 masters**
bullets: ✅|Enough to balance load and move slots
🚫|More slots would not help at that size

cols.title: ⬇ Too few
cols.text: Coarse balancing. Hard to spread data evenly.

slides.title: Say this in 1 line
slides.text: Each node sends its **slot bitmap in every heartbeat**. 16,384 slots = **2 KB** (65,536 would be 8 KB), and it still gives enough slots for clusters up to about **1,000 masters**.
